## SEPSIS WITH INTRAABDOMINAL INFECTION OR UNCLEAR INFECTIOUS SOURCE
## Consult Infectious Diseases
Empirical regimens listed below have broad coverage of likely pathogens based on
infectious site. Resistant gram-negative rods and MRSA coverage is not necessary
in most patients except those with recent isolates of these organisms. Strongly
consider rapid de-escalation of therapy in the first 24-48 hours based on MRSA
nares, isolated pathogen(s), and patient response to therapy. Refer to pathogen
specific sections of the Antimicrobial CDSS for additional treatment
recommendations.
## Empirical Treatment
Preferred:
Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q6H
Penicillin allergy:
Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h
Severe beta-lactam reaction:
Treatment of Sepsis with Severe Beta-Lactam Reaction
## Recent MRSA isolate
<ADD> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h to one of the above regimens
## Clinically unstable (ICU level care/hypotensive/tachycardic) AND recent multi-
## drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate
<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV x 1 dose to one of the above regimens
*If CrCl less than 50 ml/min: 2 mg/kg x 1 dose (use order above and modify dose)
Pharmacy to follow
## Consider abdominal CT
Abdominal CT order
## Consider selecting alternative agents from separate drug class if recently
## treated with any of the above antibiotics.

## Recent MRSA isolate
